tweets: Secunderabad, 20 August 1897: in a modest army lab, Ronald Ross dissected an Anopheles mosquito fed days earlier on a malaria patient, finding pigmented cysts studding its stomach wall. Proof, at last, that malaria travels by mosquito, not miasma.

That evening Ross wrote: 'I find thy cunning seeds, O million-murdering Death.' The discovery, made in India, won the first Nobel Prize for work done here — and 20 August is now marked worldwide as World Mosquito Day.
